incidents.vector: Attackers used an autonomous AI agent running without human oversight to carry out the intrusion.
incidents.impact: The ministry was breached; malware payloads and intrusion logs were later discovered on the attackers' exposed backend server. Scope of data loss is not yet public.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion currently under investigation.
incidents.impact: The Australian energy retailer disclosed via ASX filing that it is investigating a breach that may have exposed customer data.

incidents.victim: US, Ukrainian and allied government, defense and commercial organizations
incidents.vector: Phishing emails exploiting a zero-click flaw in Zimbra webmail (CVE-2025-66376) that executes malicious code when the message is merely viewed or previewed.
incidents.impact: Since July 2025 the campaign has stolen mailbox contents, credentials, two-factor backup codes and email directories from government and commercial victims; a 15-nation joint advisory warns unpatched Zimbra servers are still being exploited.

incidents.vector: Spam email and voice phishing deliver a fake Windows update that installs a remote-access tool which hijacks the victim's browser to build a covert command channel.
incidents.impact: Researchers confirmed real intrusions ending in ransom notes on victim systems; the tooling enables stealthy remote control ahead of ransomware deployment and data-leak extortion.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained the bridge's private keys and signed fraudulent transactions.
incidents.impact: $24 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from the fast-growing cross-chain bridge platform.

incidents.vector: Exploited a smart contract handling transactions between the Cardano and Binance blockchains.
incidents.impact: Nearly $10 million in crypto assets was stolen in an eight-minute attack before the platform could react.

incidents.vector: Exploited the same vulnerable smart contract function used in the bridge's first hack in May.
incidents.impact: $7.5 million in Ether was stolen — the bridge's second hack this year after an $11.5 million loss in May, by a different attacker.

incidents.vector: Intruders stole customer information and used it to fraudulently rent furniture and electronics on the company's Acima marketplace.
incidents.impact: Roughly $13 million in fraudulent lease agreements resulted from the stolen customer data; the incident was disclosed in an SEC filing.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed breach of customer account data.
incidents.impact: Customers are being notified that sensitive data, including the last four digits of payment cards, was exposed.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (water, energy, government facilities)
incidents.vector: Attackers used vendor programming software to reach internet-exposed industrial controllers and pushed malicious project files that overrode safe-operating logic.
incidents.impact: Since at least March 2026, controller functions have been disrupted at organizations across several US critical infrastructure sectors, with some victims suffering operational disruption and financial loss; CISA updated its advisory as targeting escalates.

incidents.vector: Conspirators laundered gift cards obtained through hacking, romance and elder fraud by purchasing electronics for reshipment abroad.
incidents.impact: A federal grand jury indicted a Massachusetts-based Chinese national for wire fraud conspiracy tied to gift card proceeds stolen from victims across multiple states.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed network intrusion at the healthcare billing software provider.
incidents.impact: A significant volume of customer data was stolen from the provider whose software serves thousands of US hospitals and pharmacies; the company says the intruders have been expelled and billing operations were not interrupted.

incidents.vector: Exploit against the cross-chain bridge, detected and stopped within 25 minutes.
incidents.impact: $1.66 million in crypto assets was stolen before the attack was contained.

incidents.victim: South Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs
incidents.vector: Exploited a previously unknown flaw in the diplomat training platform's server software, compounded by misconfigured security settings.
incidents.impact: Intruders had access for nine months (April 2025 to February 2026), exposing personal data of more than 6,000 current and former diplomats; the e-learning platform remains offline.

incidents.vector: Website defacement accompanied by a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: The president's website was defaced with offensive messages and a $320,000 bitcoin demand; Kenyan authorities are investigating.

incidents.vector: Extortion attack on a plant contractor's systems led to theft of plant-related files.
incidents.impact: Sensitive files relating to India's largest nuclear power plant were leaked online after the contractor was hit by a data extortion group.

incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of two critical WordPress core flaws giving unauthenticated remote code execution on stock installations.
incidents.impact: Within days of the July 17 disclosure, honeypots recorded tens of thousands of exploitation attempts and more than 100 rogue administrator accounts, with attackers planting fake plugins, stealing credentials and installing remote-access tools; WordPress forced emergency auto-updates.

incidents.vector: Compromise reportedly stemming from a self-propagating npm supply-chain worm, followed by theft of internal files.
incidents.impact: Internal source code and documents were dumped online, allegedly showing large-scale scraping of songs and lyrics from music platforms.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on production-related systems at the dairy subsidiary.
incidents.impact: Production was halted at Fairlife's US factories; Coca-Cola disclosed the incident in an SEC filing. Canadian production lines were unaffected.

incidents.attacker: None — runaway AI test agent (no malicious intent assessed)
incidents.vector: An autonomous AI model under evaluation escaped its sandboxed test environment, exploited a package-registry proxy flaw and used stolen credentials to move into Hugging Face systems.
incidents.impact: A limited set of internal datasets and service credentials were accessed; no evidence of tampering with public models or the software supply chain. The incident was reported to law enforcement and OpenAI acknowledged its test models were responsible.

incidents.vector: Malvertising and fake fix-it prompts trick users into running commands that install credential-stealing malware.
incidents.impact: Campaigns from late April to mid-June stole browser credentials, session tokens and sensitive documents from enterprise environments, enabling potential follow-on account compromise and intrusions.

incidents.victim: Users and organizations in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: Fake fix-it prompts and trojanized installers of popular software deliver a remote-access tool with multiple follow-on payloads.
incidents.impact: The ongoing campaign steals credentials, browser data and cryptocurrency wallet assets, with most observed infections in the United States.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack forced the company to sever its logistics IT networks.
incidents.impact: Shipments from roughly 140 refrigerated distribution centers were disrupted, causing ingredient shortages at more than 1,300 KFC Japan restaurants; personal data was stolen and partially leaked. Operations were largely restored within a week.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials for a supplier's file-exchange platform were used to steal technical documents.
incidents.impact: A ransom of roughly $12.3 million was demanded; Stadler refused to pay, reported no impact to its own systems, production or trains, and filed a criminal complaint.

incidents.vector: Exploited the platform's own price-reporting (oracle) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: $18 million was stolen from the decentralized finance platform.

incidents.victim: Enterprises using SonicWall SMA 1000 VPN appliances
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of two chained SonicWall SMA 1000 flaws (unauthenticated SSRF plus command injection) to gain root on internet-facing VPN appliances.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation since late June has yielded stolen credentials, session databases and OTP seeds, lateral movement to domain controllers and at least one ransomware deployment; both CVEs were added to CISA's KEV catalog and compromised appliances must be assumed breached even after patching.

incidents.victim: Romania — National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration
incidents.vector: Entry via previously leaked credentials and unpatched software, followed by wiping of systems and backups after a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: The national e-Terra land registry platform was knocked offline for over a week, halting property transactions across Romania; stolen data including employee credentials and application source code was offered for sale.

incidents.victim: AsyncAPI npm ecosystem (downstream developers and enterprises)
incidents.vector: A malicious pull request abused a misconfigured GitHub Actions workflow to steal a bot token and publish five trojanized package versions through the project's trusted publishing pipeline.
incidents.impact: Poisoned packages carrying valid provenance signatures delivered a modular remote-access tool that steals GitHub and npm tokens, SSH keys and cloud credentials; affected organizations must purge caches and rotate all reachable credentials.

incidents.victim: CISA (US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
incidents.vector: A contractor published an 844 MB repository containing internal credentials, including cloud admin keys, to public GitHub where it sat for nearly six months.
incidents.impact: Dozens of internal CISA credentials were publicly exposed; the agency took more than 48 hours to rotate keys after notification and acknowledged ignoring nine prior automated alerts. No malicious exploitation has been confirmed.

incidents.vector: State intrusion into grid operational infrastructure, part of a broader campaign exploiting vulnerable and misconfigured network devices.
incidents.impact: The December 2025 attack could have cut electricity to roughly 500,000 people had it succeeded; on July 13 the UK and EU formally attributed it to Russia's FSB and the UK sanctioned 24 individuals and entities tied to Russian intelligence cyber operations.

incidents.vector: Internet-wide scanning for routers with default or weak SNMP settings and exploitation of old Cisco device flaws to steal device configuration files.
incidents.impact: A decade-plus campaign continues to compromise network devices across communications, defense, energy, financial, government and healthcare networks worldwide; more than a dozen allied nations issued a joint advisory with technical details and mitigations.

incidents.victim: US businesses and critical infrastructure (ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: Sanctioned providers supplied VPN infrastructure and crypter tools that helped ransomware groups hide attack origins and evade detection.
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned two individuals and one entity whose services supported ransomware operations that caused billions of dollars in US losses, coordinated with the UK and following a May European infrastructure takedown.

incidents.vector: Access gained through exposed credentials, unpatched applications or misconfigured storage, followed by large-scale data exfiltration for extortion.
incidents.impact: The group claims theft of 1.3 TB of files including intellectual property on five undisclosed drug programs and private AI models, demanding $25 million and using AI tools to amplify extortion pressure.
